title: A/R Summary lists Emile before Émile when only the accent differs
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two customers have open invoices on today's date and their names differ only by an accent: {Customer-A} without it and {Customer-B} with it.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-07 Emile and {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-07 Émile.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Finance > A/R Summary is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Find {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} in the list.
  2. Note which one is higher.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the two customers sit next to each other.
  • Step 2: {Customer-A} (no accent) is above {Customer-B} (with the accent).

Held for the PO: the PRD says names that compare equal are ordered "by the plain lower-cased name". We read that as the lower-cased name with its accent kept, so "emile" comes before "émile". The question sheet asks Chris Ward to confirm (question 2).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R4: “Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV.”
  • S1-R3: “Accented letters sort with their base letter: "Émile's" sorts among the E names (é è ê ë sort as e, á à â ä ã å as a, ç as c, ñ as n, ö ó ò ô õ ø as o, ü ú ù û as u, í ì î ï as i, ý ÿ as y, ß as ss, æ as ae, œ as oe, in both cases).”
